thirtySeconds: KeithK75 won the Copperhead PLAYOFF at +1 net, edging HamSammich by a single stroke while IUDoc92 was the next real threat at +7. The wild part: Keith also won gross at +1, ten clear of Dan94, so this was not a handicap heist—it was a full-on demolition. His +18.63 strokes gained told the story, with huge numbers off the tee (+4.96), on approach (+6.28), around the greens (+4.49), and even with the putter (+2.91). Dan’s +8.63 SG made him the raw-game runner-up, but Keith was operating on an entirely different simulator planet.
latestTournamentTeaser: KeithK75 took the Copperhead PLAYOFF at +1 net—and also posted the best gross score by ten strokes. His +18.63 strokes gained came from basically everywhere, while the rest of the field tried to locate the fairway using sonar.

carnage.name: Leroy4522
carnage.commentary: Hole 12 was a nine-stroke expedition with no known return date. Leroy went pinestraw, rough, rough, sand, then finally green, needing seven shots just to reach a nine-foot putt before the tap-in gimmie mercifully ended the paperwork.

carnage.name: MashedBROtato
carnage.commentary: A par-3 became an eight-shot sand management seminar. The first ball found sand, the next two stayed within two yards of it, shot four wandered into rough, and then the 23-foot putt finished 13 feet away. The hole was technically completed, spiritually it was still in the bunker.

carnage.name: CRANK
carnage.commentary: Hole 12 featured the classic route: rough, pinestraw, fairway, semirough, green. CRANK finally reached a 17-footer and two-putted for an eight, proving that even +3.28 strokes gained around the greens cannot fully rescue an approach game that spent the hole filing change-of-address forms.

carnage.name: DREADFUL
carnage.commentary: Hole 11 was a par-five turned nine-shot hostage situation. After rough and pinestraw off the first two, DREADFUL needed three more wandering approaches to reach the green, then took three putts from 32 feet. The final one-foot left putt was less a miss than a formal apology.

carnage.name: HamSammich
carnage.commentary: HamSammich’s hole 5 started with 271 yards of fairway optimism and ended with an eight. The next four shots bounced through rough like they were looking for a different hole, and after finally reaching the green, a 19-footer was left one foot short. A par five became a gross triple and a net double with impressive efficiency.

carnage.name: IUDoc92
carnage.commentary: Hole 8 was a par-3 played entirely in the rough until shot four finally found the green. From there, a 17-footer became a three-footer, and the tap-in closed out a six. That is not a hole; that is 127 yards of denial followed by a small administrative putt.

carnage.name: Dan94
carnage.commentary: Hole 7 began with a 287-yard blast into sand, followed by another sand shot, followed by a shot that was still one yard from sand. Dan eventually escaped to a 25-footer and left it one foot away, turning elite tee strokes gained into a six-stroke par-four escape room.

carnage.name: KeithK75
carnage.commentary: Keith’s worst hole was a five on the par-four 16th, which is less carnage and more a minor scheduling inconvenience. The opening shot found rough, the next one went zero yards, then a 179-yard recovery reached semirough before a wedge to one foot. Even his disaster had a five-stroke limit.

players.name: KeithK75
players.tagline: **The fairway-finding missile with a one-hole speed bump.**
players.body: KeithK75 was untouchable in every version of the scoreboard, winning at +1 net and +1 gross with no net adjustment involved. The raw numbers back up the clean sweep: +18.63 total strokes gained, including +4.96 off the tee, +6.28 on approach, +4.49 short game, and +2.91 putting. He hit six fairways and nine greens, made two birdies against three bogeys, and avoided both double bogeys and three-putts. His worst hole, the par-four 16th, was still only a five despite a zero-yard second shot; a 179-yard recovery and a wedge to one foot turned potential simulator nonsense into a tap-in.

players.name: HamSammich
players.tagline: **A net grinder surviving an approach-game crime scene.**
players.body: HamSammich finished at +2 net after a 15-stroke adjustment, one shot behind the champion, while his +17 gross score showed how much work the handicap system was doing. He gained 3.63 strokes overall, with positive tee (+1.76), short-game (+0.35), and putting (+2.77) numbers, but approach fell to -1.24. Four greens, four fairways, five bogeys, and three doubles made the gross card ugly, and hole 5 was the exhibit: eight shots on a par five after a parade through rough, followed by a 19-footer left one foot short. He did find net birdies on holes 1 and 11, but the ball-striking never stopped making him earn them.

players.name: IUDoc92
players.tagline: **Approach was fine; everything within 40 yards filed a complaint.**
players.body: IUDoc92 posted +7 net from +24 gross with a 17-stroke adjustment, powered by +2.10 approach strokes gained despite a brutal -4.76 short-game number and -0.87 putting. Only three greens and 32 putts, including two three-putts, helped explain the +24 gross total, along with nine bogeys and three doubles. Hole 8 captured the problem: a 127-yard par three became a six after three straight rough-bound approaches before finally reaching the green, then a 16-footer was left three feet short. The good news was visible on holes 6 and 10, where clean pars became net birdies, but the short game spent too much of the round actively unhelping.

players.name: DREADFUL
players.tagline: **One long putt, four fairways, and zero interest in easy golf.**
players.body: DREADFUL ended at +9 net from +27 gross after an 18-stroke adjustment, with the card dragged down by -7.37 total strokes gained. The damage was broad: -2.66 tee, -2.06 approach, -0.16 short game, and -2.49 putting, plus just two fairways and three greens. Four three-putts did not help, and the par-five 11th became a nine after rough, pinestraw, more rough, and another rough approach before three putts from 32 feet. There were flashes—the two-shot birdie on 15 from 44 feet and a net birdie on 7—but the round mostly looked like a prolonged argument with the course.

players.name: CRANK
players.tagline: **Fairways hit: seven. Greens hit: one. The math is furious.**
players.body: CRANK finished +10 net on +22 gross with a 12-stroke adjustment. The short game carried the operation at +3.28 strokes gained, but approach cratered to -3.85 and putting landed at -1.25, producing -2.37 total SG. Seven fairways showed that the tee ball was not the main villain; one green in regulation absolutely was. Hole 12 was the wreckage, with rough and pinestraw off the tee, a long recovery, and an eight on the par four. Against that, the holed-out five-yard shot on 11 produced a gross birdie and a net eagle, which is a pretty effective way to briefly erase the evidence before the approach game starts something else.

players.name: Dan94
players.tagline: **Big drives, soft hands, and a short-game escape plan.**
players.body: Dan94 posted the second-best gross score at +11 and gained +8.63 strokes overall, but with no net adjustment that left him at +11 net. The raw profile was strong off the tee (+6.43), around the green (+3.10), and with the putter (+1.22), while approach slipped to -2.12. He averaged 275 yards on drives where he found fairway, made two sand saves, and recorded 27 putts with no three-putts. The trouble was the scoring leak: eight bogeys and two doubles. On hole 7, a 287-yard drive found sand, the next shot stayed in sand, and the third finished one yard from sand before a 25-footer and tap-in salvaged a six. He also made a gross birdie on the par-five first from eight feet, so the ceiling was real; the floor just had a trap door.

players.name: MashedBROtato
players.tagline: **A bunker tour with a surprisingly respectable approach department.**
players.body: MashedBROtato finished +13 net from +25 gross after a 12-stroke adjustment, with -5.37 total strokes gained. Tee play (+1.81) and approach (+0.90) were positive, but short game collapsed to -6.00 and putting added another -2.08. The card had four greens, zero recorded fairways, 34 putts, two three-putts, six bogeys, and four doubles. Hole 8 was the full-length feature: a par three that took four shots to escape the sand and rough before a 23-foot putt was left 13 feet away, followed by another putt to one foot. There were useful net birdies on holes 2 and 14, but too many recoveries turned the round into a survival game.

players.name: Leroy4522
players.tagline: **Tee to green was less a statistic than a missing-person report.**
players.body: Leroy4522 finished +17 net on +29 gross with a 12-stroke adjustment and lost -9.37 strokes overall. The entire tee-to-green profile was underwater: -3.73 tee, -3.13 approach, and -0.86 short game, with putting also at -1.65. Two fairways, two greens, 32 putts, two three-putts, four bogeys, and four doubles tell the same story. Hole 12 was the signature collapse, moving from pinestraw to rough to rough to sand before finally reaching the green in seven shots and taking a nine. The scorecard did contain a net birdie on hole 2 and a clean par on hole 4, but those were isolated sightings in a round otherwise spent negotiating hostile terrain.

stateOfLeague: KeithK75’s gross and net performance lined up perfectly, while the rest of the event showed how quickly a handicap-assisted race can tighten when raw scoring gets messy. The clearest separator was complete-game execution: Keith gained strokes in every category, while several challengers had one strong area trying to cover for major leaks elsewhere.
